title: Tech Note: Custom 4D Write Pro Navigation Panel
author: Vance Villanueva, Technical Services Engineer, 4D Inc.

historical_commentary.text: This is squarely a 4D Write Pro (the modern, object-based word processor introduced in v15) note, so the underlying premise — Write Pro as a manipulable object — remains valid, but the specific implementation relies on v17-era commands, classic form components, and C_LONGINT/C_TEXT typed declarations that predate 4D's later class-based and typed-variable (`var`) conventions. 4D Write Pro itself has continued to gain native pagination/navigation and outline features since, which may reduce the need for a fully custom navigation panel like this one.
related_updates: 4D Write Pro gained more built-in navigation, TOC, and page-thumbnail capabilities in subsequent versions
Component architecture has since evolved toward project-based components; classic form components still work but are less emphasized
C_LONGINT/C_TEXT-style declarations superseded by typed `var` declarations in v19+
